summary: Adversarial multi-agent review of the freshly built townsim V2 package
logs: Fanning out 6 module reviewers over townsim V2

findings.title: guarded_move converts do_there FAILURE into SUCCESS at the destination; broke+starving agent is stuck forever and unaffordable slots never fall back to free time
findings.description: guarded_move (core.py:185-192) is Selector([Sequence([at-location?, do_there]), go_there]). When the agent IS at the location and do_there FAILS, the Selector falls through to go_there=GoTo, and GoTo.run (nodes.py:83-87) returns SUCCESS because is_at_place() is already true. The branch therefore reports SUCCESS after doing nothing. Execution path: agent with wallet.money < 10 and needs.hunger >= 85 (hunger_critical). Root tree (trees.py:43-51): hunger emergency Condition passes -> agent walks to downtown_cafe -> EatEmergencyMeal fails (nodes.py:148-150, can't afford) -> go_there GoTo returns SUCCESS -> hunger_branch Sequence returns SUCCESS -> root Selector (trees.py:92-97) stops there. The schedule branch below is NEVER reached, so the agent never works again (EconomySystem pays only in doing_action, systems.py:396) and money is frozen; hunger only decreases via meals (_apply_start_effects) and is frozen at 100 during sleep (NeedsSystem, systems.py:84-85), so the hunger condition holds forever. The agent oscillates between standing at the cafe (root SUCCESS no-op every tick, log deduped by systems.py:47-49 so it is invisible) and the exhaustion branch's 3h sleep once fatigue creeps to 95 — an absorbing state for the rest of the run. Default content agents are wealthy enough that this needs a low-starting-money config or costlier content to trigger, but once money < 10 coincides with hunger >= 85 it is unrecoverable by construction. The same inversion has an independently reachable manifestation in the schedule branch: StartScheduledActivity returns FAILURE when the slot is unaffordable (nodes.py:120-123) and its docstring promises 'FAILURE if unaffordable so the tree can fall back to free-time behavior', but schedule_branch wraps it in guarded_move (trees.py:63-75), so at the venue the FAILURE becomes SUCCESS and the core UtilitySelector (trees.py:90, core.py:153-155) never tries the free_time child — e.g. an agent at nightlife_bar at 22:00 with money < 60 (nightlife_at_bar cost, content.py:215) stands frozen in the bar for the whole 22:00-01:00 window doing nothing, and a broke agent will even WALK to a venue it cannot pay for and freeze there. The documented affordability fallback is dead code.
findings.fix: Make the at-location failure authoritative: guard go_there with the negated location check, e.g. in guarded_move use Selector(name, [Sequence(here, [at?, do_there]), Sequence(go, [Condition(not at?), go_there])]), so do_there's FAILURE propagates out and the root can fall through to lower branches (schedule with free home meals, free time). Alternatively have GoTo return FAILURE (not SUCCESS) when invoked while already at the place inside guarded_move. The same fix restores StartScheduledActivity's documented free-time fallback (its FAILURE then correctly bubbles to the core UtilitySelector, which tries free_time as designed).

verdict.justification: Every mechanical claim verified in code and reproduced empirically. (1) guarded_move (core.py:190-193) is Selector([Sequence([at?, do_there]), go_there]) and GoTo.run returns SUCCESS when already at the place (nodes.py:83-87), so a do_there FAILURE at the destination is inverted to SUCCESS. (2) Hunger-emergency absorbing state reproduced on the real Kernel: agent with money=5, hunger=90 stayed frozen for 2 simulated days — money unchanged at 5.00 (sole income point systems.py:407 is gated on doing_action work kinds, systems.py:396-398), hunger pinned at 100 (sleeping branch systems.py:82-87 skips the hunger increment; meals are the only relief), zero wage_paid events, one 3h emergency sleep, bt_path exactly ['Root (alex)', 'Emergency: eat when starving', 'starving?', 'eat at cafe', 'walk to cafe hungry']; root Selector (core.py:117-120) returns the hunger branch's SUCCESS so the schedule branch is never reached. (3) Schedule manifestation reproduced at tree level: at the venue with an unaffordable slot (dinner_at_cafe cost 20, money 5) the root returned SUCCESS with trace ending 'walk to activity', no action started, and 'Free time' never ticked (UtilitySelector returns on SUCCESS, core.py:154-156), while StartScheduledActivity alone returned FAILURE per its docstring (nodes.py:107-108, 120-123) — the documented free-time fallback is dead code; a broke agent away from the venue walks toward it (RUNNING with move_intent). Passing tests don't contradict: test_simulation.py:85 runs 2 days at default config where agents never near the broke region (7-day default run: min money 95 across all agents, zero 'can't afford' logs), and test_behavior_core.py only tests composites with stubs, never guarded_move+GoTo. Minor inaccuracies (line citations off by a few in trees.py; 'invisible due to log dedup' overstated since interleaved conversation logs let the message reappear) don't change the finding. Severity calibrated to Major rather than Critical: the defect is unrecoverable by construction once triggered and defeats a documented fallback, but neither manifestation fires under the shipped default config/content — default agents are net cash-positive (empirically money never dropped below 95 in 7 days), so triggering requires a low-starting-money config or costlier content, which the finding itself acknowledges.

findings.title: One slow/stalled WebSocket client freezes the entire simulation (no send backpressure isolation)
findings.description: WsHub.broadcast (hub.py:80-96) loops over clients and does `await ws.send_text(payload)` sequentially. broadcast is awaited by on_tick (hub.py:75), which is awaited by the kernel tick loop at loop.py:41 (`await on_tick(kernel, events)`), so every client send sits directly on the sim's critical path. uvicorn's websockets protocol applies flow control: `send_text` blocks in `drain()` once the per-connection write buffer (~64KB) is full. Execution path: a browser tab on a suspended laptop / zero-window TCP connection stops reading -> its buffer fills within a few ticks (on_tick sends the full agent list every tick at 2.5 t/s) -> `await ws.send_text` never returns -> run_kernel stops stepping -> sim time, journal, and all OTHER dashboards freeze. Recovery relies on uvicorn's ws ping keepalive (~20s interval + 20s timeout), so each stall is up to ~40s and repeats on reconnect. Worse: a slow-but-alive reader (throttled mobile link reading slower than tick payload production) keeps answering pings, never times out, and throttles the whole simulation to its read speed indefinitely — any viewer can hang the sim. The per-client `except Exception` only helps once the connection is aborted; it does nothing against a healthy-but-slow socket.
findings.fix: Decouple broadcasting from the tick loop: give each client a bounded asyncio.Queue plus a per-client sender task; on_tick only enqueues (non-blocking). When a client's queue is full, either drop intermediate tick frames (keep latest) or disconnect that client. Alternatively wrap each send in asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=~1s) and treat timeout as a dead client.

verdict.justification: Every link in the claimed path is real. hub.py:87-90 sends to each client sequentially via bare `await ws.send_text(payload)` (no timeout, queue, or gather); hub.py:75 `on_tick` awaits `broadcast`; app.py:45-46 passes `on_tick=hub.on_tick` to `run_kernel`; loop.py:40-41 awaits `on_tick` inside the tick loop before the next synchronous `kernel.step()` (loop.py:32, kernel.py:76-104, journal write at kernel.py:101). So one blocked send halts sim time, the journal, and delivery to all other clients. requirements.txt:3 uses `uvicorn[standard]` (websockets impl with flow control: send blocks in drain() when write buffers fill; 20s ping interval + 20s timeout defaults, no overrides in cli.py:53), so a stalled reader blocks send_text for up to ~40s per stall and a slow-but-alive reader throttles the sim indefinitely — the `except Exception` at hub.py:91 only fires once the connection aborts, never on a healthy-slow socket. Tick payloads include the full agent list every tick at the default 2.5 t/s (hub.py:55, models.py:78, default.yaml:7). No test in tests/ touches the hub or websockets (grep: zero matches), so the 65 passing tests do not contradict the claim. Sole minor quibble: "buffer fills within a few ticks" understates fill time because the OS socket send buffer also absorbs data before drain() blocks (realistically seconds to a couple minutes for a dead reader), but the end state is exactly as described. Severity Critical stands: any single unauthenticated dashboard viewer can freeze or indefinitely throttle the whole simulation in the server's primary `townsim serve` mode.

findings.title: Salient-dialogue pipeline is dead code: familiarity seeded at exactly the <30 threshold and only ever increases
findings.description: InteractionSystem._process_requests marks a conversation salient only when `initiator.relationship_with(partner_id).familiarity < 30` (systems.py:314-315). But kernel.build_world seeds EVERY relationship pair (RELATIONSHIPS in townsim/config/content.py:283-302 is a full matrix over all 6 agents) with `familiarity=30.0` (townsim/kernel/kernel.py:50), and the only mutation is `rel.familiarity = min(100.0, rel.familiarity + 5.0)` on conversation end (systems.py:363) - it can never drop below 30. Therefore `salient` is always False, `conversation_ended` events never carry salient=true, Kernel.step's `narrative.on_salient_conversation` hook (kernel.py:96-100, comment 'C1') never fires, no dialogue job is ever enqueued, no `dialogue_ready` intent or `dialogue_rendered` event ever occurs, `InteractionConfig.daily_dialogue_budget` is an inert config knob, and prompts/dialogue_v1.j2 is never rendered. Verified empirically: a 2-day fake-provider run produced 6 conversations, 0 salient, 0 dialogue_rendered, min familiarity 30.0. The README advertises 'salient-encounter dialogue rendering' as a feature, and no test asserts dialogue_rendered > 0, which is why the suite (65 green tests) is green.
findings.fix: Decide the intended salience rule and make the seed/threshold consistent: either seed initial familiarity below the threshold (e.g. 20.0, or scale it by relationship type), use `<= 30`, or broaden the salience condition (e.g. `familiarity < 30 or first conversation between the pair today` / affinity-based). Add an integration assertion that a multi-day run emits at least one salient conversation and one dialogue_rendered event under the fake provider. Note: once dialogues actually fire, mid-day dialogue_ready intents apply at wall-clock-dependent ticks under paced mode, so also settle them (or timestamp their memory entries deterministically) to preserve strict-mode bit-exactness.

verdict.justification: Every link of the claim verifies. (1) systems.py:314-315 marks a conversation salient only if `initiator.relationship_with(partner_id).familiarity < 30` (strict). (2) kernel.py:47-50 seeds every relationship with `familiarity=30.0`, and RELATIONSHIPS (config/content.py:283-302) is a complete 6x6 matrix over all agents in AGENTS (content.py:245-280), so the `relationship_with` default-Relationship fallback (agents/agent.py:68-71, familiarity 0.0) is never hit for any live pair — the only conversation-request producer is behavior/nodes.py:228 between live agents. (3) A repo-wide grep shows exactly two familiarity writes: the seed (kernel.py:50) and `min(100.0, rel.familiarity + 5.0)` at systems.py:363 — monotone non-decreasing, no decay implemented (decay exists only in design docs). Hence 30.0 < 30 is false forever and `salient` is always False. (4) Downstream dead code confirmed: kernel.py:96-99 gates narrative.on_salient_conversation on the salient flag; narrative.py:112-133 is the sole producer of dialogue jobs; narrative.py:125 is the sole render site of dialogue_v1.j2; kernel.py:195-207 (dialogue_ready -> dialogue_rendered) is unreachable; daily_dialogue_budget (models.py:72) only gates salience so it is observably inert. Bonus same-root-cause dead code: the 0.9-weight 'memorable conversation' story beat at narrative.py:213 also never fires. (5) Empirical reproduction: 3-sim-day runs in the project venv at seeds 1234, 7, and 99 produced 11/10/10 conversation_ended events respectively, 0 salient in all runs, min familiarity 30.0 — matching the finding. (6) Tests: grep for salient|dialogue in tests/ returns zero matches, so the 65 green tests never cover this path; README.md:90 does advertise 'salient-encounter dialogue rendering'. Severity Major stands: an advertised LLM-dialogue feature is entirely non-functional, though nothing crashes or corrupts state.

findings.title: Scheduled 'social'/'leisure' activities freeze agents in doing_action, so no conversations can happen during the socializing windows and social need is never relieved there
findings.description: StartScheduledActivity calls _begin_action for every schedule kind, including kind='social' (socialize_at_park 20:00-22:00 in every template, party_at_bar, lunch_break_at_park). That sets state='doing_action' until the slot end (nodes.py:55-68). BehaviorSystem skips doing_action agents (systems.py:127), so ApproachAndChat never runs; InteractionSystem candidates and request validation both require state=='idle' (nodes.py:238, systems.py:304), so doing_action agents can neither initiate nor accept conversations. Kind 'social' also has no start effect (_apply_start_effects handles only meal/rest/workout, nodes.py:39-52) and NeedsSystem keeps raising social every non-sleeping tick (systems.py:87-89), while the only social relief in the codebase is _end_conversation (systems.py:359). Net effect: during the very slots named 'socialize', all agents stand still 'Hanging out and chatting' without a single conversation, social pins at 100 for extroverts, and the whole relationship/dialogue/salience pipeline only fires in small schedule gaps (~22:00-23:00, early mornings). Tests only assert started==ended counts (tests/test_simulation.py:117), which passes even with zero conversations.
findings.fix: Don't _begin_action for kind='social'/'leisure' slots (leave the agent idle at the location so ApproachAndChat can run and others can approach), or explicitly allow interaction eligibility + BT ticking for agents whose current action kind is social/leisure; alternatively apply periodic social relief during social-kind actions.

verdict.justification: Static trace and empirical execution both confirm the finding. (1) All six schedule templates in townsim/config/content.py schedule socialize_at_park (kind='social', content.py:210) at 20:00-22:00 (content.py:64,84,91,101,109,122,131,141,148,158,167). (2) StartScheduledActivity calls _begin_action for every kind (nodes.py:129), which sets state='doing_action' until slot end (nodes.py:58-60, until computed at nodes.py:128). (3) The schedule branch reliably wins utility arbitration during the slot: schedule_utility >= 1.02 even at routine_adherence=0.3 (utilities.py:16-22) vs socialize_utility max ~0.97 (utilities.py:25-35), so agents start the 'social' action instead of ApproachAndChat. (4) doing_action agents are excluded from every conversation path: BehaviorSystem skips them (systems.py:127), ApproachAndChat candidates require state=='idle' (nodes.py:238) and targets idle/moving (nodes.py:218), and InteractionSystem request validation requires both parties idle (systems.py:304-305); kernel.py:89-90 runs systems in default_systems() order (systems.py:411-413) with no other interaction path. (5) Kind 'social' has no start effect (_apply_start_effects handles only meal/rest/workout, nodes.py:39-52); NeedsSystem raises social every non-sleeping tick (systems.py:87-89); the only relief is _end_conversation (systems.py:359) plus a fitness-enthusiast workout bonus (nodes.py:51). Empirical 3-day headless run (seed 1234, default config): 10 conversations total, all at hours 7 and 22, ZERO during any 20:00-21:59 window; agent state samples during 20-22 were dominated by ('doing_action','social') (841 vs 4 idle); social need pinned at 100.0 at 20:30 for charlie, ethan, diana, fiona (alex peaked at 100 during the run). The test-gap claim is also accurate: tests/test_simulation.py:117 only asserts started==ended, which passes with zero conversations, and no test asserts a nonzero conversation count. Minor imprecisions (alex not permanently pinned at 100 at the sampled instant; a theoretical escape via reflection-shifted utility weights clamped to 0.4-2.0) do not change the substance. Severity Major is appropriate: no crash, but the simulator's core social/relationship/dialogue pipeline is suppressed during the very windows designed for it.

findings.title: Stale path + cell reservation held for hours when a walk is abandoned (GoTo early-arrival, interaction start, preemption into doing_action)
findings.description: MovementSystem.update only releases a non-moving agent's reservations when BOTH move_intent and path are empty (systems.py:148-150), but several paths leave a non-empty path or intent behind. Trace: (1) agent plans a path to reserved cell T inside a 3x3 place (systems.py:223, world/state.py:72); (2) en route it steps into another cell of the same place with waypoints remaining; (3) next tick BehaviorSystem runs before MovementSystem, GoTo sees is_at_place and returns SUCCESS, clearing move_intent and state but NOT agent.path/path_goal_key/reservation (nodes.py:82-87); (4) StartScheduledActivity puts the agent in doing_action for up to 5 hours; (5) MovementSystem skips release because agent.path is non-empty. The reservation on T blocks free_cells_in (world/state.py:65-70) and _adjacent_free_cell (systems.py:228-242) for every other agent for the whole action. Since places are only 9 cells and 6 agents converge on the cafe at meal slots, phantom reservations can empty `free`, driving path_retries to MAX_TOTAL_RETRIES, _fail, and a false "I couldn't find a way to the cafe" -> missed meals. Same leak occurs when InteractionSystem._process_requests sets state=interacting without clearing path (systems.py:318-326; AgentState.clear_transient at agents/agent.py:82-92 clears fields but never calls world.release_reservations), and when EmergencySleep/TakeRest fire while the agent is moving through the guard location (BehaviorSystem ticks moving agents, systems.py:127) — _begin_action clears nothing, so state='doing_action' with move_intent truthy also skips the release. Additionally the surviving path_goal_key+path can be reused stale on a later same-key intent (systems.py:157-159, 172-174). Self-heals only when the holder next moves with a different goal_key.
findings.fix: On any transition out of 'moving' that abandons the walk (GoTo SUCCESS, _begin_action, _process_requests conversation start), clear path/path_target/path_goal_key AND call world.release_reservations(agent.id); simplest central fix: in MovementSystem.update, for agents not in 'moving' state, always release reservations and clear path (not only when both intent and path are empty).

verdict.justification: The leak mechanism is real and exactly as cited: MovementSystem.update (systems.py:148-150) releases a non-moving agent's reservations only when BOTH move_intent and path are empty, and abandoned walks leave them non-empty. Traced and empirically reproduced: _plan reserves a random cell T in the destination place (systems.py:204, 223); 4-connected A* (pathfinding.py:18) means paths to interior cells of 3x3 places cross other cells of the same place, so the guarded_move condition (core.py:186-193) flips mid-walk; BehaviorSystem (ordered before MovementSystem in default_systems(), systems.py:411-413) then runs StartScheduledActivity/_begin_action (nodes.py:55-68), which sets state='doing_action' WITHOUT clearing move_intent/path/reservation. A headless audit (8 seeds x 5 days) found ~165-179 leaked-reservation episodes per run, observed owner states ('doing_action', move_intent truthy, 1-4 path cells remaining), held up to 361 ticks (~12 sim-hours, even longer than the claimed 5h, chaining dinner-then-sleep at the same place), including a downtown_cafe cell held 244 sim-min; it heals only on a later different-goal-key move via _clear_path (systems.py:158-159). clear_transient (agent.py:82-92) indeed never releases reservations, though the interaction-path leak self-heals one tick after conversation end via systems.py:148-150, so it is bounded by the 8-15-tick conversation. No test touches reservations/MovementSystem, so the 65 passing tests don't contradict this. HOWEVER, the load-bearing Major-severity consequence is refuted empirically: probing free_cells_in for all 12 places from every agent's perspective on every tick across 40 sim-days produced ZERO empty-free-set ticks, ZERO path_failed events, and ZERO 'I couldn't find a way' logs — the phantom reservations never exhaust the 9+ cell places with 6 agents, so no retry-exhaustion, no false failures, no missed meals. The stale-path-reuse addendum (systems.py:157-159, 172-174) exists but is benign: paths are only ever resumed from the position where they were abandoned. Real defect, but its user-visible impact is currently nil (slightly constrained target-cell choice); it is a latent hazard that would only bite with denser content (more agents or smaller places). Hence PARTIAL with severity corrected from Major to Minor.

findings.title: ApproachAndChat never consumes path_failed; MovementSystem._fail leaves move_intent set, defeating the retry backstop (chase livelock) and false-failing unrelated GoTos
findings.description: MovementSystem._fail (systems.py:185-190) sets path_failed=True, path_goal_key=None, state='idle' but does NOT clear move_intent. GoTo consumes path_failed (nodes.py:88-94) but ApproachAndChat never reads it. Path: agent chasing idle target B whose adjacent cells are all non-walkable/occupied/reserved-by-others (_adjacent_free_cell returns None, systems.py:228-242) -> after MAX_TOTAL_RETRIES=8 ticks _fail fires -> next BehaviorSystem tick, ApproachAndChat's retention branch sees the surviving move_intent (kind='agent' matches at nodes.py:231) and sets state='moving' again -> MovementSystem sees goal_key != path_goal_key(None) (systems.py:157-159) -> _clear_path RESETS path_retries to 0 -> the 8-retry cycle restarts. The MAX_TOTAL_RETRIES backstop never accumulates across cycles, so the agent loops 'Walking over to say hello' indefinitely while B stays idle and hemmed in (B can idle for hours via IdleFlavor), with the initiator's social need never relieved. Second consequence: path_failed=True persists the whole time and is consumed by whichever GoTo ticks NEXT (e.g. the schedule walk after a slot starts, or the exhaustion/hunger emergency GoTos at trees.py:36-50), spuriously failing an unrelated branch for one tick — delaying an emergency by a tick — and writing a false 'I couldn't find a way to the office' memory (nodes.py:93) for a path that was never attempted, polluting diaries/reflection prompts; the repeated plan/fail cycle also emits path_failed events every ~9 ticks that feed story beats (narrative.py:229-231).
findings.fix: In ApproachAndChat, mirror GoTo: check agent.path_failed at the top of the retention branch, consume it, clear social_target/move_intent, and return FAILURE. Also make MovementSystem._fail clear agent.move_intent so a failed intent cannot be silently re-armed, and consider making path_failed a per-goal_key token rather than a global flag so GoTo ignores failures recorded for a different goal.

verdict.justification: Every mechanical step of the claim was verified by direct code reading and then reproduced empirically with the package's real classes. (1) MovementSystem._fail (townsim/systems.py:185-190) sets path_failed=True, path_goal_key=None, state='idle' but never clears move_intent. (2) ApproachAndChat (townsim/behavior/nodes.py:206-251) contains no reference to path_failed; grep confirms the only consumers are GoTo (nodes.py:88-94) and AgentState.clear_transient (agent.py:89, called only on conversation teardown). (3) Next tick (system order Behavior->Movement per default_systems, systems.py:411-413, iterated in kernel.py:89-90), the retention branch at nodes.py:230-233 matches the surviving intent (kind=='agent') and re-arms state='moving'; MovementSystem then sees goal_key != path_goal_key(None) at systems.py:158-160 and _clear_path resets path_retries=0, so MAX_TOTAL_RETRIES never accumulates across cycles. Reproduction (real build_agent_tree + BehaviorSystem/MovementSystem/InteractionSystem, idle target whose only walkable adjacent cell is occupied by a third agent): over 200 ticks the chaser never moved, never conversed, stayed at 'Walking over to say hello', and emitted path_failed 22 times at exact 9-tick intervals — a livelock with the backstop never terminal. Second consequence also reproduced: after a _fail tick, setting hunger to 95 caused the hunger-emergency GoTo to consume the stale flag, return FAILURE, log the false memory "I couldn't find a way to the downtown cafe." for a path never attempted, and delay the emergency by one tick (the tree even fell back to the chase during that tick); narrative.py:229-231 converts each path_failed event into a story-beat candidate and path_failed is in BEHAVIORAL (events.py:16) so they feed day narration. No test covers this path (no test references path_failed, ApproachAndChat, social_target, or MAX_TOTAL_RETRIES), so the 65 passing tests do not contradict it. Only trivial imprecisions: _fail fires on the 9th failed planning tick (retries must exceed 8), the trees.py:36-50 citation is a few lines off (emergency branches are at trees.py:46-64), and the livelock is conditional on the target staying idle/moving and hemmed in — a condition the finding itself states. Severity Major is appropriate: deterministic livelock defeating a designed backstop, plus cross-branch state pollution delaying emergencies and corrupting memories/diaries/story beats, but no crash or unrecoverable state.

findings.title: Same-tick conversation request collision falsely rebuffs an agent who just entered a conversation
findings.description: _process_requests drains all requests in one tick (systems.py:297). If two requests share an agent — e.g. A requests B, and B (who targeted A or C on the same tick, both adjacent) also has a pending request — the first request starts a conversation and sets both participants to 'interacting' (systems.py:318-326). The second request is then validated with initiator.state=='interacting', fails the `valid` check (systems.py:303-305), and takes the rebuff branch: it sets social_rebuffed on the INITIATOR and journals/memorizes "<partner> seemed busy, so I let it go" (systems.py:307-309) — even though that initiator is at that moment starting a conversation (possibly with that very partner, in the mutual A<->B case where both appended reciprocal requests). Concrete trace: tick T-1 bella targets charlie while alex targets bella; tick T both are adjacent, ApproachAndChat appends (alex,bella) and (bella,charlie); (alex,bella) starts, then (bella,charlie) marks bella rebuffed and writes the false memory while she chats with alex. The stale social_rebuffed flag then kills bella's first post-conversation Socialize attempt (nodes.py:210-213), and the false log pollutes memories/diaries/story beats. Deterministic, easy to reproduce with two adjacent idle agents with high social need.
findings.fix: In _process_requests, distinguish 'initiator is no longer idle' (drop the request silently) from 'partner is busy' (rebuff); e.g. `if initiator.state != "idle": continue` before the valid check, skip any request whose initiator and partner are already interacting with each other, or dedupe reciprocal/consumed pairs before validation.

verdict.justification: Reproduced end-to-end with the real code (build_world + BehaviorSystem/MovementSystem/InteractionSystem in default_systems() order, seed 1234). Mechanism verified line-by-line: BehaviorSystem runs before InteractionSystem (systems.py:412-413); ApproachAndChat appends requests during the behavior pass (nodes.py:224-229); _process_requests drains all requests in one tick (systems.py:297); the first request (alex,bella) passes the valid check (systems.py:303-305) and sets BOTH participants to "interacting" (systems.py:318-326); the second request (bella,charlie) then fails validation because initiator bella is now "interacting", and the rebuff branch (systems.py:307-309) sets social_rebuffed on bella and writes the memory/journal entry "Charlie Davis seemed busy, so I let it go." — while charlie was actually idle and bella was at that instant starting a chat with alex (observed in the repro output at the same timestamp as "Alex Rodriguez came over for a chat."). Downstream effect also confirmed: _release (systems.py:378-384) calls only bb.leave_group and clear_transient (agent.py:82-92), neither of which clears AGENT-scope blackboard keys (blackboard.py:44-48), so the stale flag survives the conversation; on bella's first post-conversation tick with social=90 and idle adjacent candidates, ApproachAndChat consumed the flag and returned FAILURE (nodes.py:210-213), and her tree fell through to Leisure ("People-watching") instead of socializing. No test contradicts this: grep of tests/ finds no coverage of rebuff/conversation_requests/InteractionSystem; test_conversations_are_adjacent_and_symmetric only checks started==ended counts and final states, which this defect never violates. Only trivial imprecision: the finding's closing repro hint ("two adjacent idle agents") understates what is needed — the reciprocal two-agent collision is hard to reach since target selection requires the candidate to be idle; the reliable repro is the three-agent trace the finding itself gives (alex→bella, bella→charlie), which reproduced deterministically. Severity Major is appropriate: no crash or deadlock, but false memories and a spurious rebuff flag corrupt the memory stream, journal, diaries, and story inputs — the core product of this simulator.

findings.title: social_target survives preemption; agent later resumes a cross-map chase of a stale target
findings.description: UtilitySelector preemption (core.py:146-152) never resets or aborts the previously running child, and Node.reset() has no hook to undo agent-level side effects anyway; ActionExpirySystem's tree reset (systems.py:117-118) and _begin_action also leave agent.social_target untouched. Path: (1) free time, Socialize wins, ApproachAndChat picks bella within approach_radius=6 and sets agent.social_target (nodes.py:244); (2) next tick a schedule slot starts, schedule_utility (~1.2) preempts socialize+0.15 commitment, GoTo overwrites move_intent, agent works for 3 hours in doing_action (tree not ticked); (3) bella meanwhile walks across town but is 'idle' or 'moving' between slots; (4) when free time returns, ApproachAndChat's retention branch (nodes.py:216-218) sees the hours-stale target still in state idle/moving and beelines across the whole map after it — bypassing the approach_radius selection entirely, and MovementSystem's follow-replan (systems.py:167-170) will trail a target that is actively walking away. The same leak occurs intra-free-time (Leisure preempting Socialize) and via the emergency branches (rest/hunger preempting an approach, then _begin_action). Only InteractionSystem._release (clear_transient) and the target entering doing_action/interacting clear it.
findings.fix: Expire the commitment: in ApproachAndChat's retention branch, drop social_target when the target is beyond approach_radius (or record the tick it was set and expire after N ticks); additionally clear agent.social_target in _begin_action or in ActionExpirySystem alongside the tree reset.

verdict.justification: Every cited line checks out and the execution path is real. (1) ApproachAndChat's selection branch sets agent.social_target after a radius-6 scan (nodes.py:236-245; approach_radius=6 at config/models.py:71). (2) UtilitySelector preemption (core.py:147-153) resets only the child about to be ticked, never the previously running child, and Node.reset/UtilitySelector.reset (core.py:57-59, 162-164) touch only node-internal state — no hook clears agent.social_target. Preemption math verified: schedule_utility = 1.2*(0.7+0.5*0.6) = 1.2 (utilities.py:16-22) beats socialize's cap of 1.0 plus the 0.15 commitment bonus (core.py:129). GoTo overwrites the agent-kind move_intent (nodes.py:95-97) leaving social_target set; _begin_action (nodes.py:55-68) never touches it; BehaviorSystem skips doing_action agents (systems.py:127) so the tree is dormant all slot; ActionExpirySystem resets only the tree (systems.py:115-118). System order Schedule->Needs->ActionExpiry->Behavior->Movement->Interaction->Economy confirmed (systems.py:411-413, kernel.py:89-90), so the tree re-ticks the same tick the action expires. (3) The retention branch (nodes.py:215-234) accepts any target in state idle/moving (line 218) at ANY distance — no approach_radius or staleness check — and sets MoveIntent(kind="agent"), after which MovementSystem's follow-replan (systems.py:162-170) trails a target that drifts >3 cells, i.e. a cross-map chase of a possibly retreating agent. (4) The only clearing paths are exactly those the finding lists: rebuff flag (nodes.py:210-213), target busy/missing (nodes.py:218-223), conversation start (systems.py:322), and conversation-end _release->clear_transient (systems.py:378-381, agent.py:82-92). The emergency-branch variant is also real: the root Selector (trees.py:105-110) runs exhaustion/hunger/rest before core, so a threshold crossing mid-approach starts a timed action via _begin_action with social_target retained; the intra-free-time Leisure-preempts-Socialize variant is possible because socialize_utility's opportunity term collapses to its 0.2 floor while chasing a distant target (utilities.py:30-35). No test contradicts this: grep for social_target/ApproachAndChat/preempt in tests/ returns nothing; tests/test_behavior_core.py covers only UtilitySelector node semantics (commitment/fallback), not agent-level side-effect cleanup. Severity Major stands: the trigger (free time immediately followed by a schedule slot) is a routine daily occurrence, and the result — hours-stale cross-map pursuit that bypasses the deliberate locality constraint in a simulator whose core deliverable is believable behavior — is a demonstrable logic defect, though self-recovering (target becoming busy, conversation, or rebuff eventually clears it), so not Critical.

findings.title: slot_for() returns the agent's whole sleep_window for any 'sleep_at_home' override, so a reflection-proposed nap becomes an 18-hour sleep
findings.description: slot_for checks `if activity == "sleep_at_home": return agent.spec.sleep_window` BEFORE consulting schedule_overrides (townsim/agents/schedule.py:48-49). ReflectionResult.sanitized (townsim/cognition/reflection.py:34-37) allows any ACTIVITY_DATA activity in a schedule proposal, including 'sleep_at_home'. Trace: a real LLM proposes {start_hour:13, end_hour:15, activity:'sleep_at_home'}; the kernel stores the override (kernel.py:184-186); next day at 13:00 scheduled_activity returns it (schedule.py:33-35); StartScheduledActivity calls slot_for, which ignores the (13,15) override window and returns e.g. (23,7); until = ticks_until_hour(13:00 -> 7:00) = 18 hours (nodes.py:128). The agent sleeps 13:00 until 07:00 the next morning, skipping work and meals; NeedsSystem freezes hunger during sleep (systems.py:84-85) so no emergency interrupts it, and ActionExpiry is the only way out. This defeats the 'bounded feedback' guarantee of the reflection channel. FakeProvider always returns schedule_proposals=[] (providers.py:111), so no test can hit it.
findings.fix: In slot_for, check schedule_overrides (matching day/activity/window) BEFORE the sleep_at_home special case, so an override-produced sleep uses the override window; alternatively reject 'sleep_at_home' (kind == 'sleep') in ReflectionResult.sanitized so reflections cannot schedule sleep at all.

verdict.justification: Empirically reproduced end-to-end using the project's own code (venv run): a ReflectionResult with ScheduleProposal(13, 15, 'sleep_at_home') survives sanitized() (townsim/cognition/reflection.py:34-37) because 'sleep_at_home' is in ACTIVITY_DATA (townsim/config/content.py:202) and 13 != 15; the kernel stores it as agent.schedule_overrides[(next_day, 13, 15)] with no activity filtering (townsim/kernel/kernel.py:183-185), and day-rollover pruning keeps it (kernel.py:124-125). Next day at 13:00, scheduled_activity returns 'sleep_at_home' from the override (townsim/agents/schedule.py:33-35; the sleep-window precedence at 29-30 does not fire since 13 is not in (23,7)). StartScheduledActivity (townsim/behavior/nodes.py:116) calls slot_for, which short-circuits on `if activity == "sleep_at_home": return agent.spec.sleep_window` (schedule.py:49-50) BEFORE the override loop (51-53), returning (23, 7) instead of (13, 15); nodes.py:128 then computes until = ticks_until_hour(13:00 -> 7:00) = 540 ticks at 2 min/tick = 18.0 hours (verified by execution: slot_for returned (23,7), 540 ticks). During the resulting kind='sleep' action, BehaviorSystem skips agents in state 'doing_action' (townsim/systems.py:127) so no emergency branch can interrupt, NeedsSystem freezes hunger/social while sleeping (the increments are in the else branch, systems.py:82-89 — the finding cited 84-85, a two-line offset), and only ActionExpirySystem (systems.py:106) ends the action at until_tick. The test-gap claim also checks out: FakeProvider._fake_json always returns schedule_proposals=[] (townsim/llm/providers.py:111, FakeProvider class at line 66), and tests/test_reflection.py only tests unknown-activity and degenerate-window sanitization, so no passing test covers this path. Only trivial citation offsets were found (kernel.py:183-185 vs claimed 184-186; hunger freeze at systems.py:86-87 vs claimed 84-85), which do not change the described behavior. Major severity is appropriate: it breaks the module's explicitly documented bounded-feedback invariant and costs an agent up to ~18 hours of scheduled behavior, but requires a real LLM provider proposing sleep, self-recovers at the sleep-window end, and causes no crash or permanent state corruption.

findings.title: Determinism hash breaks under the default config: schedule_override_applied is hashed but lands at wall-clock-dependent ticks when strict_narrative_sync is off
findings.description: events.py puts 'schedule_override_applied' in BEHAVIORAL (townsim/kernel/events.py:18) and the journal hashes every BEHAVIORAL line including its tick (journal.py:34-37), but that event is produced by async reflection intents (kernel.py:184-189). strict_narrative_sync defaults to False (models.py:85), and the `serve` entry point has no way to enable it (cli.py:115-118 defines no --strict for serve; _apply_overrides at cli.py:41-42 leaves it False), while serve runs paced at ticks_per_second=2.5. In that default mode, narrative workers complete during the loop's real-time sleeps (loop.py:48-50) and Kernel._apply_intents (kernel.py:93, 140-148) applies reflection results at whatever tick the wall clock allows. Consequences: (a) two serve runs with the same seed and the fake provider journal schedule_override_applied at different ticks, so determinism_hash differs, violating the stated invariant (journal.py docstring lines 5-7: 'same seed and a deterministic provider produce identical hashes'); (b) worse, the reflection mutates mood, utility_weights, and schedule_overrides from that nondeterministic tick onward, so the entire subsequent behavioral event stream diverges, not just the one line. Tests only ever assert bit-exactness with strict=True (tests/conftest.py:13), so the gap is untested; the guarantee currently only holds via the CLI run path where --strict defaults on (cli.py:125-127).
findings.fix: Either make strict_narrative_sync default True (fake provider makes it free per the config comment), or move 'schedule_override_applied' (and any intent-derived event) out of the BEHAVIORAL hash set / reclassify it as NARRATIVE, or apply reflection intents only at day rollover in all modes; and scope the journal docstring guarantee to strict mode. Add a --strict flag to `serve` so the live mode can opt in.

verdict.justification: The mechanism is real but the headline consequence is impossible and the severity is overstated. Accurate: 'schedule_override_applied' is BEHAVIORAL (townsim/kernel/events.py:18), the journal hashes behavioral lines including tick (journal.py:33-37), the event is emitted only from reflection intents (kernel.py:183-188), strict_narrative_sync defaults False (models.py:85), serve lacks --strict (cli.py:115-118), and in non-strict paced mode intents land at wall-clock-dependent ticks (loop.py:48-50; kernel.py:92, 139-147); tests only cover strict=True (tests/conftest.py:13). Refuted: (1) the claimed scenario 'two serve runs with the fake provider journal schedule_override_applied at different ticks' cannot happen — the only producer (kernel.py:186) is gated on result.schedule_proposals, all reflect prompts route through complete_structured which appends 'ONLY a JSON object' (gateway.py:117-119), and FakeProvider then returns _fake_json with hardcoded "schedule_proposals": [] (providers.py:75-76, 111); sanitized() only filters, never adds (reflection.py:34-37). With a real provider the event can fire at variable ticks, but the journal docstring invariant is explicitly scoped to 'a deterministic provider' (journal.py:5-7). (2) Hash divergence between two default serve runs with the fake provider is not demonstrable: fake-provider cognition is pure CPU and completes within the first 0.4s pacing sleep after rollover, so intents land at a consistent tick (rollover+1) every run; divergence requires a >400ms stall exactly at a day boundary. (3) 'serve has no way to enable it' ignores TOWNSIM_KERNEL__STRICT_NARRATIVE_SYNC env override (models.py:108-109) and --config YAML (cli.py:111); only the CLI flag is missing. (4) models.py:81-84 explicitly documents that only strict mode gives bit-for-bit reproducibility with the narrative layer, so non-strict non-reproducibility is a documented tradeoff, not a broken invariant. Real residue: fake-provider reflections do mutate mood and utility_weights (kernel.py:176-181; agent.py:73-80), so the non-strict determinism guarantee rests on wall-clock timing rather than construction, is untested, and the journal docstring overpromises — a Minor doc/robustness gap, plus the reasonable suggestion of a --strict flag for serve.

findings.title: Semantic cache can serve one agent pair's dialogue to a different pair (corrupted memories, wrong names)
findings.description: Dialogue jobs are the only cacheable completions (townsim/cognition/narrative.py:169, cacheable=True). SemanticCache.get (gateway.py:32-43) returns the best cached response purely on prompt-embedding cosine >= threshold (default 0.97, models.py:31) with no check that the cached text belongs to the same participants. Dialogue prompts (prompts/dialogue_v1.j2) are ~80% identical boilerplate; with real OpenAI embeddings, two prompts differing only in names/moods/context routinely exceed 0.97 cosine. Execution path: pair C-D's salient conversation ends -> on_salient_conversation enqueues a dialogue job -> gateway.complete embeds the prompt, cache.get returns the dialogue previously generated for pair A-B ('Alice: ... / Bob: ...') -> Intent('dialogue_ready') -> Kernel._apply_intent (kernel.py:196-208) writes 'Conversation with {partner}: Alice: ...' into BOTH C's and D's episodic memory and broadcasts dialogue_rendered. Those false memory lines then feed the next diary prompt as the 'factual record' (narrative.py:89-97), so diaries and the town story inherit events/names that never happened to those agents. Even same-pair hits return stale dialogues referencing the wrong weekday/location. Tests only cover an exact-duplicate-prompt hit (tests/test_llm_gateway.py:87-93), so this was never exercised with near-duplicates.
findings.fix: Store participant/job metadata alongside cached values and require an exact participant match (or at least verify both current names appear in the cached text) before returning a hit; alternatively drop cacheable=True for dialogue jobs or key the cache on (a_id, b_id) plus embedding.

verdict.justification: Every code-level claim verifies. (1) Dialogue is the only cacheable completion: the sole cacheable=True call site is townsim/cognition/narrative.py:169. (2) SemanticCache.get (townsim/llm/gateway.py:35-46; finding cited 32-43, trivial drift) stores only embedding vectors and response strings and returns _values[argmax] whenever cosine >= threshold (default 0.97 at gateway.py:30; config semantic_cache_threshold=0.97 at townsim/config/models.py:31) — no participant, job-kind, or name check exists. The cache is live in production wiring (townsim/server/app.py:35, townsim/cli.py:61-72). (3) The execution path is exactly as described: systems.py:314-317 marks salient conversations, systems.py:374-376 emits conversation_ended, kernel.py:95-99 calls on_salient_conversation, narrative.py:112-133 renders dialogue_v1.j2 and enqueues, narrative.py:168-172 returns any cache hit verbatim (gateway.py:94-97) as a dialogue_ready intent, and kernel.py:195-207 writes 'Conversation with {other.spec.name}: {snippet}' into BOTH agents' episodic memories. Since dialogue_v1.j2 formats output as '{{a_name}}: ... / {{b_name}}: ...', a cross-pair hit demonstrably injects the wrong pair's names. (4) Contamination feeds diaries via narrative.py:89-97 (memories = agent.memory.for_day) and the town story via _diary_done. (5) The passing tests do not refute it: tests/test_llm_gateway.py:87-93 only tests an exact-duplicate prompt, and FakeProvider.embed (providers.py:93-95) returns SHA-256 hash vectors, so near-duplicate collisions are structurally impossible offline — the bug is scoped to the real OpenAI provider exactly as the finding states. The only element not provable from code is the empirical frequency ('routinely exceed 0.97 cosine' with text-embedding-3-small), which is plausible given that the prompts share heavy fixed boilerplate and even the variable context lines are templated log sentences differing mainly in names (systems.py:330-333, 368-370; tone is one of 3 fixed strings, narrative.py:121-122); this affects only how often the defect fires, not its existence — any non-exact hit (the cache's entire purpose) returns a dialogue wrong in names or day/time details with zero validation. Severity Major is correct: content corruption of core outputs under the real provider, no crash or kernel-determinism break.

findings.title: All OpenAI APIStatusError (including 400/401/403/404) classified as transient and retried
findings.description: OpenAIProvider._transient includes APIStatusError, the base class of ALL HTTP-status errors in the openai SDK: AuthenticationError (401), BadRequestError (400), PermissionDeniedError (403), NotFoundError (404), UnprocessableEntityError (422) as well as the genuinely transient 429/5xx. Every such error is wrapped in TransientLLMError (providers.py:47-48, 57-58) and retried by the gateway with exponential backoff up to max_attempts=4 (gateway.py:67-79). Execution path: provider='auto' resolves to openai whenever OPENAI_API_KEY (or legacy API_KEY) is set, even if the key is expired (models.py:33-39). Then every diary/reflect/story/dialogue job burns 4 API calls plus ~7s of backoff on a hopeless 401, permanently, for the life of the run (27+ jobs/day for 13 agents); a 400 context-length error from an unusually long diary prompt is likewise retried 4x and, in strict_narrative_sync mode, grinds inside the 90s rollover drain (loop.py:36-39) every single day. The embed path (gateway.py:87-89) similarly treats permanent errors as transient cache-skip conditions.
findings.fix: In OpenAIProvider, only map RateLimitError, APITimeoutError, APIConnectionError, and APIStatusError with status_code >= 500 to TransientLLMError; re-raise 4xx (except 429) as a distinct permanent error that the gateway fails fast on (and logs once, e.g. 'invalid API key').

verdict.justification: The defect is real and the execution path is exactly as described. providers.py:41 sets `self._transient = (RateLimitError, APITimeoutError, APIConnectionError, APIStatusError)`, and in the installed openai SDK 2.20.0 (_exceptions.py:104-132) APIStatusError is the base class of BadRequestError(400), AuthenticationError(401), PermissionDeniedError(403), NotFoundError(404), UnprocessableEntityError(422) as well as RateLimitError(429)/InternalServerError(5xx). providers.py:51-52 and 61-62 wrap all of them in TransientLLMError — directly contradicting that class's own docstring at providers.py:16 ("Rate limits, 5xx, timeouts — safe to retry"). gateway.py:70-74 then retries TransientLLMError with wait_exponential_jitter(initial=1, max=30) up to stop_after_attempt(max_attempts), wired to cfg.llm.max_attempts=4 (models.py:28) by both entry points (cli.py:70-71, server/app.py:33-34). models.py:36-39 confirms provider='auto' resolves to 'openai' whenever OPENAI_API_KEY or legacy API_KEY is set, with no key validation, so an expired key sends every diary/reflect/story/dialogue job into 4 API calls + ~7s backoff, permanently (narrative.py catches job failures at 141-148 so nothing fails fast or gets flagged distinctly). loop.py:36-38 awaits narrative.drain() (90s timeout, narrative.py:71) at each rollover in strict_narrative_sync mode, and gateway.py:89-92/107-112 treat the same permanent errors as transient cache-skip conditions on the embed path — all as claimed. No passing test contradicts this: tests/test_llm_gateway.py exercises retries only via a FlakyProvider raising TransientLLMError directly; OpenAIProvider's classification is never tested. Two immaterial inaccuracies: the town has 6 agents (content.py:244-281), not 13, so the daily job count is ~13 (6 diary + 6 reflect + 1 story, plus up to 4 dialogues), not "27+"; and cited line numbers are off by ~4 (wraps at 51-52/61-62, retry loop at 70-82, tuple at 41). Neither changes the mechanism or the Major severity: on any real-key run a permanent 4xx burns 4x API calls per job indefinitely with no fail-fast, and in strict mode adds a bounded (up to 90s) stall every simulated day.

findings.title: Shutdown ordering loses late-completing narrative results: intents appended during narrative.stop() are never applied (diaries/stories silently lost)
findings.description: Shutdown path: lifespan sets stop_event (app.py:50), run_kernel exits its loop and in its finally block does `await narrative.drain()` (90s internal timeout), `kernel.flush_intents()`, final on_tick, then `kernel.close()` — which closes the journal (loop.py:53-59, journal.py:47-49). Only afterwards does lifespan call `await narrative.stop()` (app.py:55), which drains up to ANOTHER 90s (narrative.py:65-69). If the first drain timed out (realistic with a real LLM: a day rollover enqueues 2 jobs per agent, gateway concurrency 4, 60s request timeout, 4 attempts — >90s backlog is easy), jobs that complete during stop()'s second drain append Intents to narrative.intents that NOBODY consumes: flush_intents already ran, the journal is closed, and lifespan never calls flush again. Diary/story text is only persisted inside Kernel._apply_intent (kernel.py:156-172 writes the .txt files), so those diaries/stories are lost entirely — the exact V1 'lost-story' failure (F04) this architecture claims to fix. cmd_run (cli.py:77-80) has the same hole: narrative.stop() after run_kernel already flushed and closed. Secondary defect on the same lines: on the 120s TimeoutError (app.py:52-54) `sim_task.cancel()` is fired but never awaited, so narrative.stop() runs concurrently with the dying task's finally block, and the CancelledError delivered inside that finally (e.g. mid-drain or mid-broadcast) skips `kernel.close()` at loop.py:59.
findings.fix: Make the caller own the terminal flush: have NarrativeCoordinator.stop() not re-drain (or return leftover intents), then in lifespan do: stop_event.set() -> await sim task -> await narrative.stop() -> kernel.flush_intents() -> kernel.close() (move close out of run_kernel's finally, or reopen-safe flush). In the TimeoutError branch, after cancel() do `await asyncio.gather(sim_task, return_exceptions=True)` before touching narrative/kernel.

verdict.justification: Primary defect confirmed by code trace and an empirical repro using the real classes. Shutdown ordering is exactly as claimed: lifespan sets stop_event (app.py:50), run_kernel's finally does drain (90s, TimeoutError swallowed with only a warning — narrative.py:74-77), then kernel.flush_intents() (loop.py:56), then kernel.close() which closes the journal (loop.py:59, kernel.py:226-227, journal.py:47-49). Only afterwards does lifespan call narrative.stop() (app.py:55), which drains up to ANOTHER 90s with workers still running (narrative.py:65-68); jobs completing in that window append Intents to narrative.intents (narrative.py:154-172) that nothing ever consumes — the only consumers are step()._apply_intents (kernel.py:92) and flush_intents (kernel.py:209-216), neither of which runs again, and diary/story text is persisted ONLY in Kernel._apply_intent (kernel.py:156-158, 167-169). cmd_run has the identical hole (cli.py:78-81). Repro (slow provider, first drain timed out): flush_intents applied 0 events, journal closed, stop() completed the diary job → 1 stranded diary_ready intent, 0 diary files on disk. The 65 passing tests do not cover this: all shutdown tests (tests/test_simulation.py:57-58,67-68,96-97,112-113) use FakeProvider, whose completions return instantly (providers.py:74-91), so drain never times out. Backlog realism checks out against config defaults (models.py:26-28: 60s request timeout, concurrency 4, 4 attempts; 6 agents × 2 rollover jobs + story + dialogues). Severity Major stands: silent loss of paid-for diary/story output on a realistic slow-LLM shutdown, in the exact failure class (F04) the architecture advertises fixing, and the second 90s drain is pure shutdown delay whose results are always discarded. One correction to the clearly-marked SECONDARY footnote: on Python 3.8+ (venv is 3.13.5) asyncio.wait_for cancels AND awaits the task before raising TimeoutError — verified empirically (task.done()=True in the except branch) — so sim_task.cancel() at app.py:54 is a no-op and narrative.stop() never runs concurrently with the dying task; the claimed consequence (CancelledError landing on an await inside run_kernel's finally skips kernel.close() at loop.py:59) remains reachable, but via wait_for's internal cancellation, and the proposed gather(sim_task) addition is unnecessary. This footnote is not load-bearing for severity or the primary fix, which is correct as proposed (caller-owned terminal flush: stop() → flush_intents() → close()).

findings.title: sim_task exception is unobserved: simulation dies silently while the server keeps serving a frozen 'connected' dashboard
findings.description: The sim runs as a bare `asyncio.create_task(run_kernel(...))` (app.py:45-46) with no done-callback and nothing awaiting it until shutdown. Execution path: any exception escaping kernel.step() or the journal write (e.g. OSError on disk-full in Journal.append/extend, journal.py:33-42, called every tick from kernel.py:102) propagates out of run_kernel and kills sim_task. Nothing logs it; the FastAPI app stays healthy, /api/state keeps answering with a frozen clock, WebSockets stay open, and the dashboard shows 'connected' with a stopped simulation and no error anywhere. The exception only surfaces at process shutdown when `await asyncio.wait_for(sim_task, timeout=120)` (app.py:52) re-raises it — which then also skips `await narrative.stop()` (app.py:55) because the shutdown block has no try/finally, leaving worker tasks to die only with the process.
findings.fix: Attach `sim_task.add_done_callback(...)` that logs the exception immediately (task.exception()), and e.g. broadcasts a 'sim_crashed' message / sets an error flag exposed via /api/state. Wrap the shutdown sequence so narrative.stop() runs in a finally regardless of sim_task's outcome.

verdict.justification: Every element of the finding is demonstrably true in the code. (1) app.py:45-46 creates sim_task via bare asyncio.create_task(run_kernel(...)) with no add_done_callback (grep: none in repo); nothing references the task again until the post-yield shutdown code at app.py:52/54, and the suspended lifespan generator frame holds a strong reference, so even asyncio's GC-time 'Task exception was never retrieved' warning cannot fire while the server runs. (2) run_kernel (loop.py:24-59) uses try/finally with no except, so any exception from kernel.step() (loop.py:32) propagates and kills the task; kernel.step() calls self.journal.extend(ctx.events) every tick at kernel.py:101 (finding says 102 — one-line drift, immaterial), and Journal.append/extend (journal.py:33-42) do unguarded file write+flush, so an OSError (disk full) escapes exactly as claimed. The only except-Exception handlers nearby (kernel.py:144-147 for intents, narrative.py:141 for jobs) do not cover step()/journal. (3) After the task dies, /api/state (app.py:69-78) keeps returning 200 with kernel.now() computed from the frozen kernel.tick, the WS endpoint (app.py:99-116) keeps looping on receive_text, and the dashboard status dot is driven solely by WS open/close (static/app.js:123, 132-134, 158-164), so it shows 'connected' with a stopped clock — a frozen simulation with no error surfaced anywhere. (4) At shutdown, wait_for(sim_task, timeout=120) (app.py:52) immediately re-raises the stored exception (task already done); the sole 'except asyncio.TimeoutError' (app.py:53) doesn't catch it, and with no try/finally, 'await narrative.stop()' (app.py:55) is skipped, leaving the 3 narrative worker tasks (narrative.py:61-63) uncancelled until process death. (5) The 65 passing tests do not contradict this: tests/test_simulation.py (lines 57, 67, 96, 112) only runs run_kernel headless with max_days; no test exercises the app lifespan, sim_task failure, or shutdown path. Severity Major is correct: the product's core function can die silently behind a fully healthy-looking server/dashboard and shutdown cleanup is skipped, but a triggering fault is required and no data corruption occurs, so it is not Critical.

findings.title: TOWNSIM_* env vars silently fail to override any key present in the YAML config
findings.description: load_config() reads the YAML file and passes it as init kwargs: `SimConfig(**data)`. In pydantic-settings, init kwargs are the HIGHEST-priority source (init > env), and sources are deep-merged per key. So any key present in the loaded YAML can never be overridden from the environment. Since townsim/config/default.yaml is always found (candidate 2) and sets kernel.seed, tick_minutes, ticks_per_second, day_start_hour, llm.provider, llm.model, needs thresholds, and server host/port, the exact examples advertised in models.py's docstring, default.yaml's header comment, and README.md line 40 (`TOWNSIM_KERNEL__SEED=7`, `TOWNSIM_LLM__PROVIDER=fake`) are no-ops. Verified empirically with pydantic-settings 2.14.2: with TOWNSIM_KERNEL__SEED=777 and TOWNSIM_LLM__PROVIDER=fake set, load_config() returns seed=42 and provider='auto', while TOWNSIM_KERNEL__STRICT_NARRATIVE_SYNC=true (a key absent from the YAML) DOES apply - which makes the bug easy to miss in spot checks. Consequence: a user who thinks they forced provider=fake via env can silently burn OpenAI credit (auto resolves to openai when a key is set), and seed 'overrides' silently don't change the run.
findings.fix: Feed the YAML through a proper settings source below env priority instead of init kwargs: override `SimConfig.settings_customise_sources` to return (init_settings, env_settings, dotenv_settings, YamlConfigSettingsSource(settings_cls, yaml_file=<resolved candidate>), file_secret_settings) - pydantic-settings >= 2.2 ships YamlConfigSettingsSource. Alternatively keep load_config but overlay parsed env values on top of the YAML dict before constructing. Add a regression test that sets a TOWNSIM_ env var for a key that IS in default.yaml and asserts it wins.

verdict.justification: Empirically reproduced in the project venv (pydantic-settings 2.14.2, pydantic 2.13.4). load_config() at townsim/config/models.py:133 passes the parsed YAML as init kwargs (`SimConfig(**data)`); in pydantic-settings, init kwargs are the highest-priority source and sources are deep-merged per key, so env vars cannot override any key present in the YAML. No townsim.yaml exists at the repo root, so townsim/config/default.yaml (candidate 2, models.py:125) is always loaded and pins kernel.seed=42, tick_minutes, ticks_per_second, day_start_hour, llm.provider=auto, llm.model, needs thresholds, and server host/port. Test run confirmed: with TOWNSIM_KERNEL__SEED=777, TOWNSIM_LLM__PROVIDER=fake, and TOWNSIM_SERVER__PORT=9999 set, load_config() returned seed=42, provider='auto', port=8000 (all env values ignored), while TOWNSIM_KERNEL__STRICT_NARRATIVE_SYNC=true (a key absent from the YAML) DID apply — exactly the asymmetry the finding describes. The advertised examples are contradicted at README.md:40, default.yaml:2-3, models.py docstring lines 4-6, and load_config's own docstring (line 122: 'env vars override'). The 65 passing tests do not contradict this: no test calls load_config() or sets TOWNSIM_* env vars (conftest.py:10 constructs SimConfig() directly). Runtime impact is real — both CLI entry points use load_config() (cli.py:51, cli.py:65), and the silent provider=auto fallback resolves to openai when an API key is set (models.py:36-39), matching the credit-burn scenario. CLI flags --seed/--provider offer a working workaround, but the documented env mechanism is silently broken for every key in the shipped default.yaml, so Major severity stands.

findings.title: pip-installed townsim is unusable: no dependencies declared, and PROJECT_ROOT-based paths break outside the repo checkout
findings.description: pyproject.toml presents townsim as an installable distribution (name/version/requires-python) but declares no `dependencies` (all runtime deps live only in requirements.txt), no [build-system], and no package-data. `pip install .` therefore installs the townsim package with zero dependencies and without static/map_data.json or prompts/*.j2 (they live at repo root, outside the package). Worse, PathsConfig defaults are anchored to `PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` (townsim/config/models.py:17), which inside site-packages resolves to the site-packages PARENT directory (e.g. .../Lib), so map_file = .../Lib/static/map_data.json does not exist. Execution path: `python -m townsim run` -> cmd_run -> Kernel(cfg) -> build_world -> TownMap.load(cfg.paths.map_file) raises FileNotFoundError at startup; and if it got further, runs_dir would write run output into the Python installation tree. Everything only works when CWD-independent PROJECT_ROOT happens to be a full repo checkout.
findings.fix: Either (a) commit to repo-checkout-only usage: add `dependencies` from requirements.txt to [project] anyway and document that townsim is not pip-installable, or (b) make it installable: add [build-system], declare dependencies, ship map_data.json and prompts as package data (importlib.resources), and make PathsConfig defaults fall back to packaged resources instead of PROJECT_ROOT. At minimum, validate cfg.paths.map_file exists with a clear error naming the expected location.

verdict.justification: The finding's factual observations are accurate: pyproject.toml (lines 1-5) declares a PEP 621 [project] table with no `dependencies`, no [build-system], and no package-data; runtime deps live only in requirements.txt; PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] (townsim/config/models.py:17) anchors PathsConfig defaults (models.py:88-91); and the cited path Kernel.__init__ (townsim/kernel/kernel.py:62) -> build_world -> TownMap.load (kernel.py:33) -> open(path) (townsim/world/grid.py:33) would raise FileNotFoundError on a missing map. However, the finding's central failure mechanic is demonstrably wrong: `pip install .` does NOT install a broken townsim. Empirical test (`pip wheel . --no-deps`, pip 26.1.2 / Python 3.13, same PEP 517 build path as pip install) fails at build time with setuptools' error "Multiple top-level packages discovered in a flat-layout: ['runs', 'static', 'prompts', 'results', 'townsim', 'behavior', 'Documents', 'simulation']" — nothing is installed, so the runtime FileNotFoundError from site-packages and "runs_dir writes into the Python installation tree" scenarios are unreachable. The misuse fails fast and loud at install time with an actionable message, not silently at runtime. Additionally, pip-installability is not a documented use case: README (lines 21, 128) prescribes `pip install -r requirements.txt` from a checkout, pyproject defines no console entry point, and the documented workflow works (65 tests pass). What remains is a real but modest packaging-hygiene gap — the [project] table implies an installable distribution that cannot actually be built, and dependencies are undeclared in project metadata — warranting Minor, not Major.

findings.title: Same-tick idle-visibility race in ApproachAndChat causes rebuff churn and false 'seemed busy' memories while the target is walking over
findings.description: BehaviorSystem ticks agents in sorted order, and ApproachAndChat's candidate filter (nodes.py:238) reads the LIVE state of agents that already ticked this pass. Trace: agent A (earlier in sort order) reaches adjacency, sets itself idle and appends request (A,B) (nodes.py:225-228); B then ticks, sees A idle, selects A as a fresh candidate and sets itself 'moving' (nodes.py:244-246); InteractionSystem then invalidates (A,B) because partner B is moving (systems.py:303-306), rebuffs A and logs 'B seemed busy, so I let it go' — while B is literally walking over to A. This costs 1-2 wasted round trips of rebuff/re-select before converging, and the social_rebuffed flag is only cleared by consumption, so it later cancels one legitimate ApproachAndChat attempt (nodes.py:210-213). (The related same-tick collision inside _process_requests itself is covered by R07.)
findings.fix: In the selection branch, when the chosen target is already within adjacency, append the conversation request immediately instead of entering the moving state; skip rebuff/log when the invalid reason is the target moving toward the initiator; and clear the social_rebuffed blackboard key in InteractionSystem._release.

verdict.justification: Empirically reproduced with the real systems in the real kernel order (Behavior -> Movement -> Interaction, townsim/systems.py:412, kernel.py:89-90). Trace verified line-by-line: BehaviorSystem ticks agents in id-sorted order (systems.py:126, state.py:49-50); initiator A at adjacency sets itself idle and appends the request (nodes.py:224-228); later-sorted B's candidate filter reads A's just-mutated live state (nodes.py:238) and the fresh-selection branch unconditionally enters 'moving' without an adjacency short-circuit (nodes.py:244-246); MovementSystem leaves agent-target movers in 'moving' on arrival (systems.py:276-286); InteractionSystem then invalidates the request because partner.state != 'idle' (systems.py:303-306), sets social_rebuffed and logs the false 'seemed busy, so I let it go' memory (systems.py:307-309) while B is walking toward A; the flag is cleared only by consumption (nodes.py:210-213) and neither _release (systems.py:378-384) nor clear_transient (agent.py:82-92) clears it, so it cancels one subsequent ApproachAndChat. A repro driving the actual BehaviorSystem/MovementSystem/InteractionSystem with alex adjacent to idle bella produced exactly this: tick 0 ends with no conversation, social_rebuffed(alex)=True, alex memory 'Bella Chen seemed busy, so I let it go.' and bella 'moving' toward alex; tick 1 converges with bella initiating (one wasted round trip demonstrated; a second is possible if the rebuffed agent's leisure branch wins first and it walks off, rebuffing the partner in turn). No passing test covers this: nothing in tests/ references social_rebuffed, ApproachAndChat, or conversation_requests, and test_conversations_are_adjacent_and_symmetric (tests/test_simulation.py:107-121) only checks started==ended and no frozen agents, which the churn does not violate. Severity Minor is appropriate: cost is ~1-2 wasted ticks, one false low-importance memory per occurrence, and one cancelled approach; the conversation still starts via the partner.

findings.title: rest_spot blackboard entry is only deleted on TakeRest success, making a preempted choice sticky indefinitely
findings.description: rest_spot_for (nodes.py:191-198) chooses a spot once and stores it AGENT-scoped; only TakeRest.run deletes it (nodes.py:171). If the rest branch is preempted after the choice but before TakeRest runs — e.g. the tired condition (fatigue>=70) holds, the walk to the chosen spot begins, then hunger crosses 85 mid-walk and the higher-priority hunger branch (trees.py root order) takes over, ending in a meal action and a tree reset that never touches the blackboard — the entry persists. Days later, the next tired episode reuses the remembered spot regardless of where the agent now is, e.g. walking across town to downtown_cafe when central_park is adjacent. Bounded (one key per agent, value always valid), no determinism impact, but it silently changes the 'choose per rest episode' semantics implied by TakeRest's delete, and Blackboard.clear_agent is never called anywhere to clean it up.
findings.fix: Delete the AGENT-scoped rest_spot key whenever the rest branch exits without completing (e.g. clear it in ActionExpirySystem/tree-reset paths, or store the tick with the spot and re-choose when stale/too far).

verdict.justification: The mechanical claims are all code-true: rest_spot is chosen once and stored AGENT-scoped (townsim/behavior/nodes.py:194-197), the sole delete in the codebase is TakeRest.run at nodes.py:171, hunger preemption mid-walk is possible (BehaviorSystem ticks "moving" agents at townsim/systems.py:127; root Selector is reactive, townsim/behavior/core.py:114-122; priority order exhaustion>hunger>rest>core at townsim/behavior/trees.py:105-110), ActionExpirySystem's tree reset never touches the blackboard (systems.py:115-118, core.py:57-59), and Blackboard.clear_agent (blackboard.py:40) is never called in production code. However, the headline scenario is misdescribed: in the given hunger-preemption example the key does NOT persist "days later" or "indefinitely." Fatigue is only reduced by TakeRest or sleep (systems.py:84-85, nodes.py:45-47), so when the 30-minute meal expires the tired condition (fatigue>=70) still holds, the rest branch — which strictly outranks the schedule/core — immediately re-fires, the agent walks to the remembered spot, and TakeRest deletes the key; the episode self-heals, and resuming the same spot is arguably intended episode-resumption. True multi-day staleness requires the episode to end without TakeRest ever running, which only happens in a narrow sub-case: fatigue crossing fatigue_exhausted=95 during the preemption (requires fatigue >= ~93 when preempted, at 0.05/min gain) triggering EmergencySleep, or a GoTo path-failure fallback (nodes.py:88-94). Even then the impact is weaker than the example implies: the original choice is a proximity-blind 50/50 rng draw between central_park and downtown_cafe (nodes.py:196), so "walking across town when central_park is adjacent" is equally likely with a fresh draw — stale reuse merely replaces a new uniform draw with the previous one. Real state-hygiene defect, but the "sticky indefinitely" mainline is overstated; Minor severity stands (it is already the lowest tier).

findings.title: Dialogue budget checked and charged only for the conversation initiator, and charged for non-salient conversations
findings.description: Salience (which gates LLM dialogue rendering) is decided at conversation start from the initiator only: 'initiator.daily_dialogues_used < daily_dialogue_budget' (systems.py:314), and at conversation end the counter increments only for conv.a ('if me.id == conv.a', systems.py:365-366) regardless of whether the conversation was salient. Two consequences: (1) the partner's budget is never consumed nor checked, so one popular agent can appear in up to budget*(N-1) LLM dialogues per day as a partner, defeating the per-agent budget intent documented at models.py:72; (2) the initiator's budget is consumed by every conversation they initiate, including non-salient ones with familiar partners, so an agent who chats with 4 friends in the morning gets no LLM dialogue for a genuinely salient first meeting later that day.
findings.fix: Increment daily_dialogues_used only when conv.salient is true, increment it for both participants, and check both agents' budgets in the salience predicate at systems.py:314.

verdict.justification: Both claimed behaviors trace exactly to the code. (1) Salience is computed solely from the initiator at systems.py:314-315 ('initiator.daily_dialogues_used < ctx.cfg.interaction.daily_dialogue_budget and initiator.relationship_with(partner_id).familiarity < 30'); the partner's budget is never checked anywhere. (2) At conversation end, systems.py:365-366 increments daily_dialogues_used only when 'me.id == conv.a' and unconditionally with respect to conv.salient — and conv.a is always the initiator because world/state.py:87-92 new_conversation preserves argument order from systems.py:316. The salient flag really does gate LLM dialogue rendering (kernel.py:96-99 dispatches narrative.on_salient_conversation only for salient conversation_ended events), and the budget is per-agent per-day (reset at kernel.py:121; documented intent at models.py:72). Consequence 1 verified: conv.b is never charged, so an agent can partner in up to budget*(N-1) salient LLM dialogues/day. Consequence 2 verified concretely: configured friendships start at familiarity 30.0 (kernel.py:50), so friend chats are non-salient yet still charge the initiator; after 4 such chats (budget=4), a first meeting with a stranger (default familiarity 0.0, components.py:57) fails the budget check and gets no LLM dialogue. No test covers this — grep for salient/dialogues_used/dialogue_budget in tests/ returns zero matches, so the passing suite is silent. Severity Minor is correct: it misallocates LLM rendering budget but does not affect simulation correctness or determinism.

findings.title: Memory entries of kind 'summary'/'reflection' are never compacted — unbounded linear growth in long-running servers
findings.description: compact_before keeps every entry with kind in ('summary','reflection') forever (memory.py:72-81). The day rollover adds one 'summary' per agent per day (kernel.py:127-137) and each nightly reflection adds up to 3 'reflection' entries per agent (kernel.py:190-193). Nothing ever prunes these kinds, so agent.memory.entries grows linearly without bound for the lifetime of a `townsim serve` process (roughly 4+ entries/agent/day). Prompt size stays bounded because on_day_end slices summaries[-6:] (narrative.py:90), so the impact is process RAM, the summaries() linear scan at every rollover, and snapshot/API payloads (memory_size in /api/agents), not prompt drift — but it is genuinely unbounded growth the 2-day tests cannot see.
findings.fix: Cap or roll up summaries/reflections in compact_before (e.g. keep only the newest N per kind, or fold summaries older than compact_after_days into a single rolling summary).

verdict.justification: Every claim verifies against the code. (1) memory.py:75-78 — compact_before's keep-filter unconditionally retains entries with kind in ("summary","reflection"); this is the only code in the package that ever removes memory entries, so those kinds are never pruned. (2) kernel.py:126-136 — each day rollover (once day_index exceeds compact_after_days=2, models.py:105) appends one new kind="summary" entry per agent via compact_before(cutoff, summary). (3) kernel.py:189-192 with reflection.py:24/:32 — each nightly reflection (one reflect job per agent per rollover, narrative.py:110) adds up to 3 kind="reflection" entries. Net: ~4 never-pruned entries/agent/day, unbounded for the lifetime of a `townsim serve` process (cli.py:115). (4) Impact scoping is accurate: narrative.py:90 slices summaries()[-6:] so prompts stay bounded; the cost is process RAM, linear scans in summaries()/for_day()/retrieve() (memory.py:44-58), and the memory_size field in /api/agents (server/app.py:91). (5) Passing tests don't contradict it: test_simulation.py:88-89 only bounds kind=="event" entries over a 2-day run, and test_memory.py:61-71 asserts summaries survive compaction — the very behavior causing the growth. Trivial line-number drift in the finding (kernel.py 127-137/190-193 vs actual 126-136/189-192) is immaterial. Minor severity is appropriate: no incorrect behavior, bounded prompts, and the leak (~4 small entries/agent/day) only matters for very long-running servers.

findings.title: Scored retrieval subsystem and MemoryConfig scoring knobs are entirely unwired
findings.description: MemoryStream.retrieve (memory.py:49-70) is never called anywhere in townsim (grep confirms the only occurrences are its definition), MemoryEntry.embedding is never populated (no code path ever assigns it, and LLMGateway.embed at gateway.py:104-109 has no callers), so the advertised Generative-Agents recency/importance/relevance retrieval never influences any prompt — diary/reflect prompts use raw for_day()/summaries() slices instead (narrative.py:89-107). Additionally, AgentState builds MemoryStream via default_factory (agents/agent.py:44), so the MemoryConfig fields alpha_recency, beta_importance, gamma_relevance, recency_decay_per_tick and retrieve_k (config/models.py:100-104) are silently ignored: changing them in townsim.yaml has no effect, which is misleading dead configuration rather than a runtime fault.
findings.fix: Either wire it up (construct MemoryStream from cfg.memory in build_world, embed important entries via gateway.embed off the tick path, and use retrieve() to select prompt context) or delete retrieve(), the embedding field, and the unused MemoryConfig knobs to stop advertising behavior that does not exist.

verdict.justification: Every element verified by direct trace. (1) MemoryStream.retrieve (townsim/cognition/memory.py:49-70) has zero callers in townsim — grep finds only the definition plus unit tests (tests/test_memory.py:36,43,50,57), so the 65 passing tests exercise the method in isolation and do not contradict the wiring claim. (2) MemoryEntry.embedding is never populated: all four construction sites (systems.py:50-53, kernel/kernel.py:133-135, 190-192, 202-205) omit embedding=, and LLMGateway.embed (gateway.py:107-112; claim cited 104-109, off by 3 lines — immaterial) has no callers (provider.embed is used only for the semantic cache inside gateway.complete at gateway.py:88-104, unrelated to memory relevance).
